personas.name: Fast-Track Felix
personas.experience: Intermediate with Claude Code, expert in domain
goals: Solve immediate problem without reading documentation
Find the RIGHT plugin, not browse hundreds
Install quickly and start using within 30 seconds
Trust that plugin won't break existing workflow
pain_points: Too many similar plugins - which one is maintained?
Installation breaks something else (dependency hell)
Plugin doesn't work - no clear troubleshooting
Can't find plugin for specific framework (e.g., 'LangGraph debugging')

behaviors.search_strategy: Problem-first ('how to debug LangGraph workflows'), not category-first
behaviors.trust_signals: Download count, last updated date, verified badge

quotes: I don't have time to read 14 agent descriptions - just tell me which one fixes my problem
If installation requires reading a README, I'm out
I need to know it won't conflict with my existing setup BEFORE installing

scenarios.happy_path: Search 'LangGraph debug' -> See workflow-architect agent (5000+ installs, updated yesterday) -> Click install -> Auto-activates on .langgraph files -> Tooltip shows new command
scenarios.edge_case: Searches 'React testing' -> Finds 3 similar plugins -> Comparison view shows differences in approach/coverage -> Chooses based on team needs
scenarios.failure_mode: Installs 'test-generator' agent -> Conflicts with existing test setup -> No rollback option -> Manually removes files -> Gives up on plugins

personas.jtbd: When I encounter a development problem I haven't solved before, I want to find and install a proven solution in under 2 minutes, so I can get back to building my feature.

personas.name: Builder Bianca
personas.experience: Expert with Claude Code, wants to share expertise
goals: Package internal agents/commands for team reuse
Get credit/recognition for solving common problems
Maintain plugin with minimal ongoing effort
Understand who's using it and how
pain_points: Don't know plugin packaging format/requirements
Unclear how to handle dependencies (skills that reference other skills)
Publishing process is manual and error-prone
No feedback loop - are users finding bugs?

behaviors.maintenance_tolerance: Willing to fix bugs, not rewrite for every Claude Code update

quotes: I built this workflow-architect agent for my team - others probably need it too
I don't want to become a support channel - the plugin should be self-documenting
If publishing requires 20 steps, I'll just share a Gist instead

scenarios.happy_path: Finishes agent -> Runs 'claude publish agent workflow-architect' -> Auto-validates structure -> Prompts for description/tags -> Publishes to marketplace -> Gets download notifications
scenarios.edge_case: Agent depends on custom skill 'langgraph-patterns' -> Publish wizard detects dependency -> Offers to bundle or require separate install -> Creator chooses bundle for simplicity
scenarios.failure_mode: Publishes agent -> Users report bugs -> No update mechanism -> Creator abandons plugin -> Users stuck on broken version

personas.jtbd: When I've solved a problem that others face, I want to package my solution as a discoverable plugin in under 30 minutes, so I can help the community without ongoing maintenance burden.

personas.name: Governance Gary
personas.experience: Limited Claude Code experience, high security requirements
goals: Control what plugins team can install (whitelist/blacklist)
Host private plugins for proprietary workflows
pain_points: No visibility into what plugins are installed
Plugins could leak proprietary code/data
No way to enforce company standards
Breaking changes break CI/CD pipelines

behaviors.duration: Full day to review and configure

quotes: I need a private marketplace - public plugins are a non-starter
Show me what data this plugin accesses before I approve it
If a plugin update breaks our build, I need instant rollback

scenarios.happy_path: Sets up private Claude Code registry -> Curates 20 approved plugins -> Team can only install from approved list -> Auto-updates controlled via policy -> Quarterly security review
scenarios.edge_case: New plugin request from team -> Gary reviews code/permissions -> Approves with restrictions (can't access secrets) -> Plugin runs in sandbox mode
scenarios.failure_mode: Developer installs unapproved plugin -> Plugin exfiltrates API keys -> Security incident -> Complete ban on Claude Code plugins

personas.jtbd: When my team wants to use Claude Code plugins, I need centralized control and visibility over installations, so I can enable productivity without compromising security or compliance.

journey_maps.scenario: Installing first plugin to solve urgent problem

actions: Encounters unfamiliar error in LangGraph workflow
Thinks 'there must be an easier way to debug this'
stages.thinking: I bet there's a plugin for debugging LangGraph workflows
pain_points: Doesn't know if plugin marketplace exists
Unclear how to access it
opportunities: In-editor suggestion: 'Install workflow-architect agent to debug LangGraph issues'
Command palette: 'Search plugins...' (Cmd+Shift+P)

stages.thinking: Which one actually solves my problem? Are any of these good?
pain_points: All descriptions sound similar
Can't tell which is maintained/popular
No preview of what commands/features are added
opportunities: AI-powered ranking: 'Top match for LangGraph debugging' badge
Rich metadata: '5.2k installs, updated 2 days ago, 4.7 stars'
Preview tooltip: 'Adds commands: debug-workflow, trace-state, visualize-graph'
Comparison view: Side-by-side feature matrix of top 3 results
key_moments: First 3 search results determine if user finds solution

stages.thinking: Will this break my existing setup? Is it trustworthy?
stages.feeling: Cautious (risk of breaking things), impatient (wants to try it)
pain_points: No clear indication of what will change in workspace
Dependency list is technical jargon
Can't try before committing to install
opportunities: Impact summary: 'Adds 4 commands to Command Palette, watches .langgraph files'
Plain-English dependencies: 'Requires sequential-thinking skill (auto-installed)'
Sandbox mode: 'Try in temporary workspace' button
Verified badge: 'Reviewed by Claude team' for security/quality

stages.feeling: Anxious (during wait), relieved (on success), curious (what's new)
pain_points: No indication of what's happening during install
Success message doesn't explain what changed
Unclear how to start using new features
opportunities: Real-time status: 'Downloading... Validating dependencies... Installing...'
Interactive success: 'workflow-architect installed! Try: @workflow-architect debug my graph'
Guided first use: 'Click here to run your first debug command' (tooltip)
Changelog preview: 'What's new in v2.1.0' (if upgrade)

stages.thinking: This is exactly what I needed! How did I not know about this before?
pain_points: Doesn't know about other features plugin offers
No record of having installed it (for future reference)
opportunities: Feature discovery: 'workflow-architect can also: trace state, visualize graph'
Plugin journal: 'Installed plugins' view shows all active plugins + features
Share success: 'Share this plugin with your team' (one-click)

stages.thinking: If it ain't broke, don't fix it. But what's new?
stages.feeling: Satisfied (with current version), curious (about update), cautious (breaking changes?)
pain_points: Update notification interrupts workflow
No clear indication if update is critical or optional
Fear of breaking changes
opportunities: Smart notifications: Only notify for critical updates, batch minor updates weekly
Traffic light system: Green (safe), Yellow (new features), Red (breaking/security)
Preview changes: 'See what's new' inline preview before updating
Auto-rollback: 'If issues occur, auto-rollback to v2.1.0 after 24 hours'

critical_moments: First 10 seconds of search - if top 3 results aren't relevant, user gives up
Install button click - must feel safe, not risky
First use - must be obvious how to activate new features
Update notification - must not create anxiety about breaking things

stages.thinking: Other teams probably need this. Should I publish it?
pain_points: No clear path from 'local agent' to 'published plugin'
Doesn't know marketplace standards/requirements
opportunities: Publish suggestion: When agent reaches maturity (usage threshold), prompt 'Share workflow-architect with community?'
Guided wizard: 'Publish Agent' command walks through requirements
Template validation: Auto-check against plugin standards before publish

stages.thinking: Am I doing this right? What if I'm missing something?
pain_points: Manual creation of manifest (error-prone)
Unclear what fields are required vs optional
No validation until publish attempt
opportunities: Auto-generate manifest: 'claude package agent workflow-architect' creates manifest from agent metadata
Interactive form: CLI prompts for name, description, tags, version with examples
Live validation: Red/green indicators as fields are filled, with helpful error messages
Dependency auto-detection: Scans agent for skill references, prompts to bundle or require

stages.thinking: I should test this before publishing. How do others test plugins?
pain_points: No official way to test plugin in isolation
Hard to simulate fresh install experience
No automated validation of plugin structure
opportunities: Test mode: 'claude test-plugin ./workflow-architect' creates temporary isolated environment
CI/CD template: Auto-generated GitHub Actions workflow for plugin validation
Automated checks: Validates agent structure, command syntax, dependency resolution
Sandbox preview: Spins up Claude Code instance with ONLY this plugin installed

stages.thinking: How long until it's live? Did I do everything right?
pain_points: Opaque review process - no status visibility
Long wait times (if manual review required)
Rejection without clear fix instructions
opportunities: Instant publish for simple plugins: Auto-approve if passes all checks, no code review needed
Staged rollout: Publish to 'beta' tier first, graduate to 'stable' after 100 installs + no bugs
Review dashboard: Real-time status of review process with checklist
Auto-fix suggestions: 'Your README is missing installation instructions - add this section:...'

actions: Gets bug report via GitHub issue
stages.thinking: People are using it! But now I'm on the hook for support.
pain_points: No built-in feedback mechanism (users open random GitHub issues)
Hard to gauge user satisfaction beyond install count
No way to communicate with users (e.g., announce breaking changes)
opportunities: Analytics dashboard: Installs over time, active users, command usage frequency, error rates
In-plugin feedback: Users can rate/review directly from Claude Code, issues auto-create GitHub discussions
Creator newsletter: Opt-in to receive weekly digest of user feedback + analytics
Deprecation path: 'Mark as deprecated' -> users notified -> recommend alternative -> sunset date

critical_moments: Decision to publish - if process looks hard, creator won't bother
Package preparation - manual steps = high abandonment rate
Publishing - long wait = frustration, seek alternative (Gist, private repo)
First bug report - if no easy fix/update path, creator abandons plugin

stages.thinking: What are the risks? How do we mitigate without blocking productivity?
pain_points: No clear documentation of plugin permission model
Unclear what data plugins can access
No reference policy templates for enterprises
opportunities: Enterprise docs: Dedicated section on security model, permissions, sandboxing
Permission transparency: Every plugin declares permissions upfront (file access, network, secrets)
Policy templates: 'Conservative', 'Balanced', 'Open' preset policies for different risk profiles
Risk assessment tool: Auto-score plugins based on permissions, code complexity, maintainer reputation

actions: Configures Claude Code to use private registry
stages.thinking: This is complex. Do we have the resources to maintain this?
pain_points: Private registry requires server infrastructure + maintenance
Complex configuration (HTTPS, auth, mirroring)
No guidance on hybrid model (private + curated public)
opportunities: Managed private registry: Claude offers hosted private registry (like npm Enterprise)
Configuration wizard: 'claude enterprise init' sets up private registry + team config
Hybrid mode: 'Allow public plugins with auto-approval rules' (e.g., verified publishers only)
Zero-config option: Policy file in repo auto-enforces rules without infrastructure

stages.thinking: How do I know which ones are safe? This is taking forever.
pain_points: Manual code review of every plugin is unsustainable
No trust signals beyond download count
Unclear maintenance status (abandoned plugins?)
opportunities: Verified publisher program: Plugins from verified orgs get trust badge + expedited approval
Automated security scans: Static analysis detects common vulnerabilities, shown in UI
Maintenance signals: 'Last updated 6 months ago - consider alternatives' warning
Curated collections: 'Enterprise-approved' collection pre-vetted by Claude security team
Bulk approval: 'Approve all plugins from @anthropic' rule for trusted publishers

stages.thinking: Is the team frustrated? Are we blocking them from being productive?
pain_points: No visibility into blocked install attempts (users fail silently)
Team doesn't understand why plugins are blocked
Request approval process is manual/slow
opportunities: Transparent blocks: When user tries unapproved plugin, shows reason + request approval button
Auto-request workflow: User clicks 'Request', sends to Gary with context, Gary approves in Slack
Analytics dashboard: Gary sees 'Top 10 requested plugins this month' -> proactive approvals
Educational messaging: 'This plugin requires file system access - your org requires approval for security'

stages.thinking: Which plugins are actually being used? Which are abandoned?
pain_points: No usage analytics (approved but never installed?)
Breaking changes in plugin updates affect team
Manual process to notify team of deprecated plugins
opportunities: Usage insights: 'workflow-architect: 45 active users, test-generator: 2 active users (consider removing)'
Update policies: 'Auto-approve minor updates, require review for major versions'
Deprecation automation: When plugin marked deprecated, notify users + suggest alternative
Health score: Each plugin gets health score (maintenance, security, usage) -> auto-flag at-risk plugins

critical_moments: Initial research - if security model unclear, project dies here
Infrastructure setup - if too complex, Gary chooses 'block all plugins' instead
First blocked install - if user experience is bad, team rebellion against policy
Quarterly review - if too manual, Gary stops doing it -> stale/insecure plugins accumulate

user_stories.story: As a developer encountering a new problem, I want to search for plugins by my problem description, so I can find relevant solutions without learning plugin categories
acceptance_criteria: Search understands natural language queries (e.g., 'debug LangGraph workflow')
Results ranked by relevance to query, not just keyword match
Top 3 results show metadata: install count, last update, rating, verified badge
Search completes in < 500ms with results visible above-the-fold
user_stories.impact: HIGH - Primary discovery mechanism for 80% of users
user_stories.effort: MEDIUM - Requires semantic search + ranking algorithm

success_metrics.metric: Search-to-install conversion rate
Time from search to finding relevant result
Search abandonment rate

user_stories.story: As a developer considering a plugin, I want to see what changes it will make to my workspace before installing, so I can avoid breaking my existing setup
acceptance_criteria: Plugin detail page shows 'Impact Summary': commands added, file watchers, dependencies
Plain-English dependency descriptions (not just package names)
Conflict detection: warns if plugin conflicts with installed plugins
'Try in Sandbox' button lets user test plugin in isolated environment
user_stories.impact: HIGH - Reduces installation anxiety, increases trust
user_stories.effort: MEDIUM - Requires dependency analysis + sandbox environment

success_metrics.metric: Install-to-immediate-uninstall rate
Plugin detail page bounce rate
User-reported 'broke my setup' issues

user_stories.story: As a developer who just installed a plugin, I want guided first-use instructions, so I can start using new features immediately without reading docs
acceptance_criteria: Post-install notification shows example command or usage snippet
Tooltips on new Command Palette items explain what they do
Optional interactive walkthrough: 'Try your first debug command'
Persistent 'What's new' indicator until user tries new feature
user_stories.impact: MEDIUM - Reduces time-to-value, increases feature discovery

success_metrics.metric: Users who use plugin within 1 hour of install
Users who discover > 50% of plugin features in first week
Plugin uninstall due to 'didn't know how to use'

user_stories.story: As a developer with installed plugins, I want smart update notifications that don't interrupt me, so I can stay current without constant distractions
acceptance_criteria: Critical updates (security, breaking bugs) show immediate notification
Minor updates batched into weekly digest notification
Update notification shows traffic light: Green (safe), Yellow (new features), Red (breaking/critical)
One-click update with auto-rollback if issues detected within 24 hours
user_stories.impact: MEDIUM - Reduces notification fatigue, maintains security
user_stories.effort: MEDIUM - Requires update classification + rollback system

success_metrics.metric: Update notification dismissal rate
Users running outdated plugins (> 3 months old)
Updates causing user-reported breakage

user_stories.story: As a developer managing multiple plugins, I want a Plugin Manager view showing all installed plugins and their features, so I can understand and control my enhanced environment
acceptance_criteria: Plugin Manager shows: installed plugins, active/inactive status, version, install date
Each plugin expandable to show: commands added, skills included, file watchers, dependencies
Bulk actions: disable all, update all, export plugin list
Usage stats: 'Last used 3 days ago' or 'Never used - consider removing'
user_stories.impact: MEDIUM - Helps users manage growing plugin collection
user_stories.effort: MEDIUM - New UI view + usage tracking

success_metrics.metric: Users who use Plugin Manager at least monthly
Plugins uninstalled due to 'didn't know I had it'
Average plugins per user

user_stories.story: As a plugin creator, I want a simple CLI command to publish my plugin, so I can share my work without manual packaging
acceptance_criteria: 'claude publish agent <name>' command validates and publishes in one step
Interactive prompts for: description, tags, version, license
Auto-generates manifest.json from agent/command/skill metadata
Dependency auto-detection: scans for skill references, prompts to bundle or require
user_stories.impact: HIGH - Primary creator enablement, reduces 70% of publish friction

success_metrics.metric: Time from 'decide to publish' to 'live in marketplace'
Publish success rate (vs abandonment)
Creators who publish multiple plugins

user_stories.story: As a plugin creator, I want to test my plugin in isolation before publishing, so I can catch bugs and ensure quality
acceptance_criteria: 'claude test-plugin ./my-agent' creates temporary isolated environment
Simulates fresh install: no existing plugins, clean workspace
Automated validation: checks agent structure, command syntax, dependency resolution
Sandbox preview: spins up Claude Code instance with ONLY this plugin for manual testing
user_stories.impact: HIGH - Improves plugin quality, reduces post-publish bug reports

success_metrics.metric: Plugins with bugs reported within first week
Creators who test before publishing
Average time to first bug fix after publish

user_stories.story: As a plugin creator, I want instant publishing for simple plugins and staged rollout for complex ones, so I can iterate quickly without waiting for manual review
acceptance_criteria: Plugins passing all automated checks auto-publish to 'beta' tier immediately
Beta plugins visible with 'Beta' badge, users can opt into beta plugins
After 100 installs + no critical bugs for 7 days, auto-graduate to 'stable' tier
Complex plugins (code execution, network access) require manual security review

user_stories.effort: HIGH - Requires tiered system + automated checks

success_metrics.metric: Publish wait time for simple plugins
Publish wait time for complex plugins
Security incidents from auto-published plugins

user_stories.story: As a plugin creator, I want analytics and feedback on my plugin usage, so I can prioritize improvements and understand my users
acceptance_criteria: Creator dashboard shows: installs over time, active users (last 30 days), command usage frequency
Error rate tracking: which commands are failing, with stack traces
User feedback: in-plugin rating/review system, auto-creates GitHub Discussions for issues
Weekly digest email: 'workflow-architect had 50 new installs, 4.8 star average, 2 new issues'
user_stories.impact: MEDIUM - Helps creators improve plugins, increases quality over time

success_metrics.metric: Creators who check dashboard at least monthly
Plugins with > 100 installs that are maintained (updated in last 3 months)
Creator response time to bug reports

user_stories.story: As a plugin creator updating my plugin, I want to communicate breaking changes clearly to users, so they can prepare and don't get surprised
acceptance_criteria: Version bump to 2.0.0 triggers 'breaking change' workflow
Creator writes migration guide: 'What changed, how to update your usage'
Users see update as 'Red (Breaking)' notification with migration guide link
Option to delay update: 'Remind me in 1 week' or 'Stay on v1.x until manually updated'
user_stories.impact: MEDIUM - Reduces user frustration from unexpected breakage
user_stories.effort: LOW - UI enhancements + version check logic

success_metrics.metric: Breaking change updates causing user complaints
Users who read migration guide before updating
Plugin uninstalls due to breaking changes

user_stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want transparent plugin permissions before approval, so I can make informed security decisions
acceptance_criteria: Every plugin declares permissions in manifest: file access (read/write/paths), network access, secret access, command execution
Plugin detail page shows permissions prominently with risk indicators
Permission comparison: 'This plugin requests MORE permissions than similar plugins'
Admin can approve plugins with restricted permissions: 'Allow, but deny network access'
user_stories.impact: HIGH - Enables enterprise adoption, blocks if missing

success_metrics.metric: Enterprise admins who feel confident approving plugins
Security incidents from approved plugins
Time to review and approve plugin

user_stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want a managed private plugin registry without infrastructure burden, so my team can use plugins securely
acceptance_criteria: Claude offers hosted private registry (like npm Enterprise): $X/user/month

success_metrics.metric: Enterprise customers using private registry

acceptance_criteria: Every plugin auto-scanned for: hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, XSS, dependency vulnerabilities

Curated 'Enterprise-Approved' collection: Claude team pre-vets popular plugins for security
user_stories.impact: HIGH - Reduces manual review burden by 80%
user_stories.effort: HIGH - Security scanning pipeline + verification program

success_metrics.metric: Plugins approved without manual code review
False positive rate (scan incorrectly flags issue)
Security vulnerabilities in approved plugins

user_stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want visibility into plugin usage and request approvals, so I can proactively manage the plugin ecosystem
acceptance_criteria: Admin dashboard shows: approved plugins, active users per plugin, blocked install attempts
Request approval workflow: user clicks 'Request', Gary approves in Slack/email
'Top 10 requested plugins this month' report guides proactive approvals
Usage insights: 'workflow-architect: 45 users, test-generator: 2 users (consider removing)'
user_stories.impact: MEDIUM - Improves admin efficiency, balances security with productivity

success_metrics.metric: Average approval time for plugin requests
Approved plugins with zero usage
User satisfaction with approval process

user_stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want automated update policies and deprecation management, so plugins stay secure without constant manual work
acceptance_criteria: Update policies: 'Auto-approve minor/patch updates, require review for major versions'
Deprecation automation: when plugin marked deprecated, notify users + suggest alternative
Health scoring: each plugin gets health score (maintenance, security, usage) -> auto-flag at-risk
Quarterly review assistant: 'These 5 plugins need attention (outdated/unused/vulnerable)'

success_metrics.metric: Admin time spent on plugin management per quarter
Plugins running outdated versions with known vulnerabilities
Plugins deprecated without user notification
